newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says to protect Nissan Life policyholders.
newsitem.headline: MOF says to protect Nissan Life policyholders.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Friday that the ministry will protect all policyholders of Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co Life, which it ordered earlier to halt some of its operations.
"It is natural for us to protect all policyholders," Mitsuzuka said.
In a statement, the ministry said it ordered the Japanese life insurance firm at 9 a.m. (0000 GMT) on Friday to halt operations such as making or cancelling contracts.

Mitsuzuka told a regular news conference that the ministry had received a report from Nissan Life that it had come to a decision to discontinue business at an emergency board meeting held earlier on Friday.
"After receiving the report, I thought it was my duty as finance minister to deal with the problem in a swift manner and eliminate any worries," Mitsuzuka said.
He said the ministry was preparing to announce who would manage the company's insurance policies and added that the life insurance association would likely become involved.
But he added that further discussions would be held on how to transfer insurance policies to other companies.
Mitsuzuka said Nissan Life's failure was due to its failed asset management, but added that there would be no similar cases with other life insurance companies.
"I've heard that a direct cause of Nissan Life's failure was its failure in managing assets. There is not such a similar case in other companies."
Mitsuzuka said it was the first failure of a Japanese life insurance company in the postwar period, adding: "I hope to make it the last."
